text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Philips and three other electronics groups agree on joint licensing of digital video disc (DVD) technology (page 1).
- Groningen-based builder Koop Tjuchem acquires German pipeline-laying firm Suedrohrbau in deal which will almost double Dutch firm's annual turnover to 1.4 bln guilders (p1). VOLKSKRANT
- Samsung Aerospace willing to pay up to $150 million to acquire failed Dutch plane-maker Fokker.
- Researchers at Philips and Eindhoven technical university set new record for transmission of data via optic fibre: 10 gigabytes per second.
- Nine out of 10 Dutch companies are not yet taking any practical measures to prepare for planned launch of single European currency. DE TELEGRAAF
- Main Dutch trade union federation FNV to press for three percent wage increase in 1997 pay negotiations. ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- Government puts pressure on General Audit Chamber not to publish report criticising state financial support to companies. TROUW
- Almost half of all Dutch workers now have an official 36-hour working week.
